subject: Post-call: RAG eval & retrieval/reranker recommendations for Ferrolytics
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call: RAG eval & retrieval/reranker recommendations for Ferrolytics

Thanks for your time today — quick recap and proposed next steps from our end. High level notes:

- Use case: Customer support knowledge base augmentation (mix of short FAQs and long technical KB pages).
- Primary objective: Improve grounding and reduce hallucination on multi-paragraph KB pages while keeping 95th pctile latency under 450ms for question-answering flows.
- Current constraints: On-prem data store (S3-compatible), sensitive diagrams (PII redaction in metadata), expected throughput ~120 qps at peak.

Immediate recommendations (what we promised on the call):
1) Retrieval settings: hybrid BM25 + sparse neural retriever (dense) with an initial top_k=50 retrieval then rerank down to top_k=5 for generation. We suggested caching vector lookups for repeated prefixes.
2) Reranker: experiment with a lightweight cross-encoder reranker quantized to int8 for latency budget; fallback to a bi-encoder re-ranking + lexical score if load spikes.
3) Candidate models: prefer a 7B high-quality open model for generation (cost/latency) and keep a 13B or 34B as a cold-fallback for edge-case correctness checks.
4) Eval plan: run two prompt-set passes (FAQ-style and multi-paragraph Q/A) plus adverse queries designed to probe hallucination. We'll measure grounding precision@k, hallucination rate (hallucinations per 100 responses), and token cost.

Attachments: I uploaded an initial prompt set and a sketch of the reranker profile (attached).

Next steps / asks for Ferrolytics:
- Can you confirm a sample export of 10k anonymized KB documents (S3 path) by next Tue?
- Please share any hard SLAs for 95/99 latency or retention constraints.

Internal: looping in Rishi and Marissa to propose an eval plan, sample config, and a rough cost estimate (tokens + infra). We'll aim to have a scoped PoC plan by EOW (Fri).

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Post-call: RAG eval & retrieval/reranker recommendations for Ferrolytics

Thanks — digging into the technical ask and putting a concrete PoC blueprint below. Quoted Camila's summary for context:

> Use case: Customer support KB augmentation. Objective: reduce hallucination while keeping p95 latency < 450ms.

Proposed PoC blueprint (technical):
- Indexing / retrieval:
  - Vector store: customers prefer on-prem S3 + open vector-db; we'll supply embedding microservice that runs in VPC and writes to the vector index. Use dense vectors (512 dim) from an on-prem embedder we recommend (small 1.5B embed model) to avoid egress.
  - Retrieval pipeline: initial retrieval top_k=50 (approximate ANN) -> lexical re-score (BM25) -> cross-encoder rerank to top_k=5. If load > 100 qps, degrade gracefully to top_k=20 + bi-encoder re-rank.
- Reranker choice:
  - Candidate: cross-encoder based on a distilled 110M cross-attention model (fast to run on A10G-like hardware, quantized int8) — target latency ~30–60ms per rerank for top50 -> top5 (batched).
  - Fallback: bi-encoder with asymmetric scoring pre-computed, useful for high-throughput tails.
- Generation models: start with an instruction-tuned 7B (q4_0) for baseline; warm-up with a 13B (q3_k) if a question triggers low confidence (low grounding score).
- Grounding metric definitions:
  - grounding_precision@5 = (# grounded answers where generated cite overlaps with returned top5 docs) / (# total eval queries)
  - hallucination_rate = (# hallucinated answers flagged by raters) / 100 responses; track drift across weekly runs.

Eval matrix (what we'll run):
- 2 prompt sets: FAQ short-answer (3k queries) and Long-form explanation (1k queries).
- For each, run 3 model configs (7B baseline, 13B cold-fallback, and 7B + cross-encoder rerank) and measure grounding_precision@1/3/5, hallucination_rate, p95 latency, and token cost.

Operational notes:
- Reranker on VPC: yes — cross-encoder binary and weights can be packaged into a container image and run in Ferrolytics' VPC with Redwood sidecar for telemetry. We'll provide a hardened container and a compliance checklist for KMS usage.
- Cache policy: prefix cache for repeated question stems; TTL 12h by default.

Deliverables & timeline:
- Mon: receive sanitized S3 export.
- Wed: Redwood shares initial index plan, and an eval runbook + prompt set mapping. (Attachment: ferrolytics-retrieval-config.yaml)
- Fri EOW: scoped PoC cost estimate + running small eval (1k queries subset).

I've attached the proposed reranker profiles and a small retrieval config sample. Internal action: Marissa/Dylan, please draft the eval runbook and rough infra cost (GPU hours) today so Camila can confirm commitment.

— Rishi
